title: Who Owns the Archive?
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: Who Owns the Archive?: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: A fashion archive is not one asset. It is a governed constellation of physical objects, copyrights, marks, contracts, files, testimony, privacy interests, access permissions, and institutional obligations.
frames.alt: Title plate for Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: The record separates the material dress, House of Worth attribution, Charles Frederick Worth design credit, accession, and the museum’s present custody.
frames.credit: Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of the Brooklyn Museum, 2009; Gift of the Princess Viggo in accordance with the wishes of the Misses Hewitt, 1931
frames.alt: Ivory and blue silk evening dress with a fitted bodice, deep neckline, and long trained skirt, designed by Charles Frederick Worth around 1882.
frames.treatment: local display and download with attached credit

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · INVENTORY — What is actually here?. Assign a persistent identifier to each object, file, recording, agreement, credential, and related record. Preserve original order and provenance before reorganizing for convenience.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what is actually here? within Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · SEPARATE — Which interest attaches to which item?. Record physical title, copyright authorship and transfers, trademark or design records, contract limits, privacy, access, and conservation separately. One accession row may need several rights rows.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping which interest attaches to which item? within Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · GOVERN — Who may possess, use, reproduce, lend, digitize, describe, and dispose?. Turn vague control into verbs, responsible parties, territory, term, approval, exceptions, recovery, and a source document. Unknown is a valid status; guessed ownership is not.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who may possess, use, reproduce, lend, digitize, describe, and dispose? within Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · STEWARD — What must remain usable after a transfer?. Require identifiers, checksums, condition notes, formats, contextual narration, rights evidence, audit history, and a correction route to travel with the archive.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what must remain usable after a transfer? within Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: Fragmenting the archive into rights can obscure its cultural wholeness; treating it as culturally whole can obscure the rights and labor of photographers, makers, sitters, donors, employees, and communities. Ethical stewardship must keep both views in frame.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for Who Owns the Archive?.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery

frames.caption: For each, separate custody, material title, copyright, contract, privacy, access, and conservation evidence.
